_about: Mark Talks Health shared study library. One verified entry per study. Blog articles cite these by key ([^key]); the documentary builder, social studios and courses should read the same file so every channel says the same thing. 'finding' is a plain-language summary in Mark's voice (never a quote). 'caveat' is the honest limit of the study and must be shown wherever the study is used. 'verified' is the date the citation details were checked against the journal or an indexed record. Add a pmid only when it has been confirmed; otherwise links fall back to a PubMed search by DOI.

sperber2021.authors: Sperber AD, Bangdiwala SI, Drossman DA, et al.
sperber2021.title: Worldwide Prevalence and Burden of Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders, Results of Rome Foundation Global Study
sperber2021.finding: About 4 in 10 adults surveyed online, and about 1 in 5 interviewed at home, met the medical criteria for at least one functional gut disorder such as IBS. Those people reported worse physical and mental quality of life and saw doctors more often.
sperber2021.caveat: Survey data: it measures how common symptoms are, not what causes them.

vanuytsel2014.authors: Vanuytsel T, van Wanrooy S, Vanheel H, et al.
vanuytsel2014.title: Psychological stress and corticotropin-releasing hormone increase intestinal permeability in humans by a mast cell-dependent mechanism
vanuytsel2014.finding: Giving a stressful public speech made healthy volunteers' guts measurably leakier, but only in people whose cortisol rose. Injecting the stress hormone CRH caused the same effect, and a drug that calms mast cells blocked it.
vanuytsel2014.caveat: Small study in healthy people over a short window; it shows stress can open the gut barrier, not that it causes long-term disease.

david2014.authors: David LA, Maurice CF, Carmody RN, et al.
david2014.title: Diet rapidly and reproducibly alters the human gut microbiome
david2014.finding: Switching people to an all-animal or all-plant diet changed their gut bacteria within days. The animal-only diet boosted bile-loving microbes, including Bilophila wadsworthia, and lowered the fibre-fermenting species.
david2014.caveat: Short, extreme diets in a small group; it shows how fast the microbiome responds, not which long-term diet is best.

wastyk2021.authors: Wastyk HC, Fragiadakis GK, Perelman D, et al.
wastyk2021.title: Gut-microbiota-targeted diets modulate human immune status
wastyk2021.type: Randomised trial, 36 healthy adults, 17 weeks in total (10-week diet phase)
wastyk2021.finding: Adults who added fermented foods such as yogurt, kefir, kimchi and kombucha steadily grew more diverse gut bacteria, and 19 inflammation proteins in their blood fell, including interleukin-6. The high-fibre group's diversity stayed flat on average and those 19 markers did not fall.
wastyk2021.caveat: Small trial in healthy adults at Stanford; the fibre group's response depended on the bacteria they started with, so fibre still matters.

mihaylova2018.authors: Mihaylova MM, Cheng CW, Cao AQ, et al.
mihaylova2018.title: Fasting Activates Fatty Acid Oxidation to Enhance Intestinal Stem Cell Function during Homeostasis and Aging
mihaylova2018.finding: A single 24-hour fast boosted the regenerative power of intestinal stem cells in both young and old mice by switching them over to burning fat for fuel.
mihaylova2018.caveat: Mouse study; it has not been shown in human guts yet.

rangan2019.authors: Rangan P, Choi I, Wei M, et al.
rangan2019.title: Fasting-Mimicking Diet Modulates Microbiota and Promotes Intestinal Regeneration to Reduce Inflammatory Bowel Disease Pathology
rangan2019.type: Animal study (mice) plus a small human pilot, USC (Valter Longo lab)
rangan2019.finding: In mice with colitis, repeated 4-day cycles of the fasting-mimicking diet lowered gut inflammation, increased intestinal stem cells, grew protective bacteria such as Lactobacillus and reversed intestinal damage. A water-only fast helped some markers but did not reverse the damage. In a human pilot, FMD cycles lowered markers of whole-body inflammation.
rangan2019.caveat: The gut repair was shown in mice; the human data are a small pilot on inflammation markers, not an IBD treatment trial.

maifeld2021.authors: Maifeld A, Bartolomaeus H, Löber U, et al.
maifeld2021.title: Fasting alters the gut microbiome reducing blood pressure and body weight in metabolic syndrome patients
maifeld2021.type: Randomised trial, 71 adults with metabolic syndrome
maifeld2021.finding: People who did a 5-day fast before starting a healthy (DASH) diet saw their gut bacteria shift sharply, with more of the species linked to lower blood pressure. Three months later they had lower blood pressure, a lower BMI and needed less blood pressure medication than people who did the diet alone.
maifeld2021.caveat: Supervised fast in a clinical setting in people with metabolic syndrome; not a guide for unsupervised long fasts.

allen2018.authors: Allen JM, Mailing LJ, Niemiro GM, et al.
allen2018.title: Exercise Alters Gut Microbiota Composition and Function in Lean and Obese Humans
allen2018.type: Human exercise study, 32 previously inactive adults
allen2018.finding: Six weeks of supervised cardio, 30 to 60 minutes three times a week, changed people's gut bacteria and raised gut-protective short-chain fatty acids such as butyrate in lean participants. When they stopped exercising for six weeks, most changes faded.
allen2018.caveat: The short-chain fatty acid rise was seen in lean but not obese participants, and the changes needed ongoing exercise.

smith2019.authors: Smith RP, Easson C, Lyle SM, et al.
smith2019.title: Gut microbiome diversity is associated with sleep physiology in humans
smith2019.type: Observational study, 26 healthy men, 30 days of sleep tracking
smith2019.finding: Men with more diverse gut bacteria slept more efficiently, slept longer and woke up less during the night.
smith2019.caveat: Small, men-only and correlational: it shows sleep and gut diversity travel together, not which one drives the other.

gaylord2011.authors: Gaylord SA, Palsson OS, Garland EL, et al.
gaylord2011.title: Mindfulness training reduces the severity of irritable bowel syndrome in women: results of a randomized controlled trial
gaylord2011.type: Randomised controlled trial, 75 women with IBS
gaylord2011.finding: Women with IBS who did an 8-week mindfulness course cut their symptom severity by about 26% straight after, and about 38% three months later, compared with about 6% and 12% in a support group.
gaylord2011.caveat: Women only; mindfulness was compared with a support group, not with medication.

thoma2013.authors: Thoma MV, La Marca R, Brönnimann R, et al.
thoma2013.title: The effect of music on the human stress response
thoma2013.finding: Women who listened to relaxing music before a stress test had their nervous-system stress marker (salivary alpha-amylase) return to normal faster than women who sat in silence.
thoma2013.caveat: Mixed result: cortisol actually rose most in the music group, and heart rate and felt stress did not differ. Music helped recovery, it did not block stress.

hunter2019.authors: Hunter MR, Gillespie BW, Chen SY
hunter2019.title: Urban Nature Experiences Reduce Stress in the Context of Daily Life Based on Salivary Biomarkers
hunter2019.type: Real-life study, 36 city dwellers over 8 weeks
hunter2019.finding: Spending time in nature lowered the stress hormone cortisol by an extra 21% per hour on top of its normal daily fall. The best return per minute came from 20 to 30 minutes outside.
hunter2019.caveat: Small study measuring stress markers, not gut outcomes directly.
